What is the equation of the ellipse given above?

{{field-1}}$=1$
worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=6$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{6}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{36}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
